correctness.rationale: Jaccard and squared Ochiai are strictly decreasing functions of the exact keys u and u+v. This gives a complete algebraic reversal criterion. Two independent finite-domain constructions and exact rational comparisons certify the first weak split at richness 3 and the unique first strict reversal at richness 5; the infinite family is proved symbolically.

evidence: Jackson, Somers and Harvey directly compare Jaccard and Ochiai on fish presence–absence data and report different sensitivity to occurrence-frequency or size effects.
Pavoine's full text places Jaccard and Ochiai in a common community-similarity framework, gives their matching-component formulas, and compares their behavior on theoretical and empirical data.
The literature establishes that the coefficients are not interchangeable empirically, but does not give the finite ordering boundary.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Empirical differences and pointwise formula comparisons motivate the problem but do not imply a necessary-and-sufficient cross-ranking condition or a smallest integer Venn witness.

originality.rationale: Published ecology literature owns the Jaccard and Ochiai coefficients, their presence-absence formulas, and empirical evidence that they respond differently to occurrence-frequency structure. The inspected sources and targeted searches did not state the exact cross-comparison criterion, the sharp first strict-reversal boundary, the unique first pair, or the displayed infinite family.
residual_risks: The Jackson 1989 full article itself was not fully inspectable through the publisher route; only its abstract and public author-upload record were available.
The reversal criterion is algebraically elementary once the standard formulas are written together, so an unindexed note or software test may contain an equivalent observation.
The theorem concerns binary pairwise community similarity only and does not cover abundance-weighted or generalized Ochiai/Jaccard constructions.

value.rationale: Jaccard and Ochiai are established ecological similarities whose differing occurrence-frequency behavior is documented in the literature. The exact ordering criterion identifies when that difference changes an actual ranking, while the sharp five-species boundary and persistent family supply minimal, reproducible benchmark cases rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
